data.one_liner: Flutter plugin to expose Android Intents to Dart, including initial and new intents, and return results.
data.what_it_does: It forwards the Intent that started the Flutter activity to Dart, and streams any subsequent Intents received while the activity is running. It also exposes caller info and allows sending a result back to the originating activity.
use_when: You need to handle deep links or app links on Android
You want to receive share intents or any custom intent actions
You need to return a result to an Android activity that started Flutter for result
avoid_when: You only need to handle standard deep links (uni_links covers that)
You need cross-platform intent handling (iOS not supported)
strengths: Full access to Android Intent data, including extras, action, categories, and component info
Provides a stream for real-time intent handling
Supports returning results to the calling activity
weaknesses: Requires manual intent-filter configuration in AndroidManifest
No code generation or declarative API
data.setup_notes: Add intent-filter to AndroidManifest.xml, import package, call ReceiveIntent.getInitialIntent() and listen to ReceiveIntent.receivedIntentStream. No build_runner needed.
